identity.title: Ejection History of the IRAS 04166+2706 Molecular Jet

paper_type_evidence.quote: Aided by numerical simulations in the framework of unified wind model by Shang et al. (2006), the observed velocity pattern can indeed be generated.

evidence.quote: the first highly collimated, extremely high velocity bipolar outflow identified in the nearby Taurus molecular cloud (140 pc)
the first highly collimated, extremely high velocity bipolar outflow identified in the nearby Taurus molecular cloud (140 pc)

question.value: Can the saw-tooth velocity pattern of the IRAS 04166+2706 molecular jet be explained by a spherically expanding wind with axial density concentration, and what does it imply for the ejection history?

evidence.quote: This pattern can be formed by a spherically expanding wind with axial density concentration.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00304.S.
CO $J=$ 2 – 1, SiO $J=$ 5 – 4 and SO $J_N =$ $6_5$–$5_4$ transitions were observed simultaneously
The array was in its C$32-2$ configuration and no observations with the compact Morita Array were made
the beam-size of the CO data is $1.5\ensuremath{''}\times1.1\ensuremath{''}$.

observing_dates.value: December 2014 (ALMA data of Tafalla et al. 2017)

evidence.quote: observed the two knots B6 and R6 of the I04166 outflow at 230.5 GHz using ALMA in December 2014.

provided.value: CO J=2-1 PV diagram of the whole jet (with single-dish data added), compared with the model

evidence.quote: Single-dish data were added to the visibility to improve the quality of the CO $J=$ 2 – 1 images, and the beam-size of the combined data is $3\ensuremath{''}$.

provided.value: CO J=3-2 data of inner knots (Wang et al. 2014)

evidence.quote: The CO $J=$ 3 – 2 data of (cite: wang2014) taken in 2010 by the SMA covered the inner four pairs of knots

what.value: ALMA CO J=2-1 observations of knots B6 and R6 and inclination estimate of 38 deg from the plane of the sky

evidence.quote: This is the average angle estimated by (cite: tafalla2017) based on the elliptical shapes of the knots B6 and R6 in their ALMA observations.

what.value: PdBI CO J=2-1 PV diagram and data provided by the authors

evidence.quote: We thank M. Tafalla and J. Santiago-García for providing the CO $J=$ 2 – 1 data of the molecular outflows IRAS 04166$+$2706.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: 2D axisymmetric unified wind model simulations with two-temperature scheme, synthetic CO J=2-1 PV diagrams and channel maps

evidence.quote: Our simulations build upon the unified wind model framework outlined in (cite: shang2006) with detailed simulation setups following the two-temperature generalization described in (cite: wang2015).

what.value: Simulation setup follows the two-temperature generalization

evidence.quote: detailed simulation setups following the two-temperature generalization described in (cite: wang2015)

unstated_but_needed: Simulation code name, grid and resolution not given
Exact velocity values per burst not tabulated
Coordinates of the source and the knot positions/velocities picked from PV diagrams
ALMA calibration and imaging details (in Tafalla et al. 2017)

method.value: Derive the tooth slope on the PV diagram vs. inclination for a spherical wind layer; overlay on observed CO 2-1 PV with 28, 38, 48 deg

evidence.quote: At each knot position, we overlay three sets of velocity pattern computed with different inclination angles on top of the observed CO $J=$ 2 – 1 data.
we display the model pattern up to a half-opening angle of $\alpha=7.5$$^\circ$ from the rough center of each tooth.
The overall behavior of the whole sawtooth velocity pattern can therefore be generally explained with one same inclination angle

method.value: Manually pick two points per tooth, compute eta-hat and theta; error from shifting a point by 140 AU

evidence.quote: we displace the upper selected point in each pattern to the left and right by 140 AU

analysis_steps.goal: Numerical simulations with variable velocity history

method.value: Unified wind simulations with burst or low-high cycle velocity history; synthetic PVs convolved with 3" beam

evidence.quote: each having a constant speed and lasts for $20$ years long.

key_parameters.value: period ~93 yr; M_A=150; T=100 K; inclination 52 deg from line of sight; inner cone 3 deg

evidence.quote: We adopt a large Alfvén Mach number of $M_A=150$ for purposes of better modeling.

assumptions.value: Level populations in statistical equilibrium, radiative effects ignored; line width 1 km/s

evidence.quote: For simplicity, effects of radiative excitation and de-excitation on the level populations were ignored so the line emissions can be calculated locally.

fitting.value: Velocity histories designed by hand to fit

evidence.quote: The velocities of the ejecta are designed so as to let them travel ballistically to the observed location by the time of $t=0$.

validation.value: Compare convolved synthetic PV and channel maps with observations

evidence.quote: Although not perfectly, our numerical simulations successfully reproduce the observed velocity pattern.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean inclination from plane of sky, blue lobe

evidence.quote: The mean inclination angle values are $38.4$$^\circ$ and $37.6$$^\circ$ for the blue and red shifted lobes

results_numeric.quantity: Mean inclination from plane of sky, red lobe

evidence.quote: The mean inclination angle values are $38.4$$^\circ$ and $37.6$$^\circ$ for the blue and red shifted lobes
The value of $\hat{\eta}$ falls in the range of $\sim-3$ to $-1$.
we will try to follow a periodicity of $\sim93$ year, which is estimated from the roughly equal spacing of the first few knots
The dynamical age of the fitted regions (up to knots B7 and R7) is about 1200 years.

findings_qualitative.value: Outer knots are well described by thin spherical shells; inner knots retain velocity history and need continuous variation

evidence.quote: the more evolved outer knots are indeed well described by the model of thin spherical shell.

claims.hypothesis: A spherical wind with axial density concentration explains the sawtooth PV pattern
claims.experiment: Analytic projection model compared with CO 2-1 PV diagram
claims.result: One inclination of ~38 deg fits most knots
claims.finding: The pattern is a projection effect of a wind-like velocity field

evidence.quote: The overall agreement implies that the proposed geometric model does capture the feature of the I04166 jet kinematics.

claims.hypothesis: The unified wind model can reproduce the pattern
claims.experiment: Simulations with bursty or cyclic velocity history, synthetic PVs
claims.result: Observed sawtooth reproduced, though not perfectly

evidence.quote: Numerical simulations in framework of the unified wind model can successfully reproduce the sawtooth-like velocity pattern observed in the I04166 molecular jet.

claims.hypothesis: Inner knots follow the same simple slope relation
claims.finding: The simple model is incomplete for inner knots

evidence.quote: The decreasing inferred $\theta$ from inner to outer knots, however, is puzzling as it appears too systematic to be random measurement errors.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Jet with internal working surface side-way ejection cannot be ruled out, but it does not naturally explain the coherent slope variation

evidence.quote: although this does not rule out the possibility of a jet shock.

limitations_admitted.value: Axisymmetric model cannot represent asymmetric knot B6; knot B7 not reproduced

evidence.quote: The asymmetric knot is not well represented by the current axisymmetric model.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data are only used indirectly via Tafalla et al. 2017 and PdBI data
Velocity histories are hand-tuned, so fits are not unique
Model is qualitative with no quantitative goodness of fit

missing_for_reproduction: Digitized PV data and picked points
reproducibility.score_reason: Mainly theory and simulation with unreleased code; ALMA data enter only through earlier publications.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are simulation-based and the recipe is incomplete.

companion_papers.why: ALMA observations of knots B6 and R6
PdBI CO and SiO maps of the outflow
